title: Practice · Joining sentences
description: Join two sentences with {qui}, {que}, {où} and {dont}, say what you like with {ce que}, plan round the weather with {si}, and invite, accept, refuse and thank.
can_do: Say what you like or find hard with {ce qui} and {ce que}
Make a plan that depends on the weather, and answer an invitation

items.instruction: Léa tells Maya who lives where. Join the two sentences with {qui}.
items.shown: Le monsieur habite au premier étage. Il a un chien.
items.answer: Le monsieur qui habite au premier étage a un chien.

mistakes.answer: Le monsieur que habite au premier étage a un chien.
mistakes.feedback: The man does the living, so the verb comes next: {qui habite}.

items.text: La météo dit qu'il va pleuvoir samedi prochain. ___ pleut, on va à la bibliothèque.
items.gloss: The forecast says it will rain next Saturday. If it rains, we'll go to the library.

items.text: L'immeuble ___ j'habite est vieux, mais il est sympa.
items.gloss: The building I live in is old, but it's nice.

mistakes.feedback: A building is a place, and Léa lives there: {où}.

items.instruction: Maya has been here a week. Say it with what she likes first. Start with {Ce que}.
items.answer: Ce que j'aime surtout, c'est le quartier.
accept: Ce que j'aime, c'est surtout le quartier.

mistakes.answer: Ce qui j'aime surtout, c'est le quartier.
mistakes.feedback: A subject comes next, {je}, so it is {ce que}.

items.shown: Léa lit un livre. Le livre est très long.
items.answer: Le livre que Léa lit est très long.

mistakes.answer: Le livre qui Léa lit est très long.
mistakes.feedback: A new subject comes next, {Léa}, so the word is {que}.

items.text: Je vous ___, madame, mais je ne peux pas venir samedi.
items.gloss: Léa to Madame Garnier, who has invited her for tea: Thank you, madame, but I can't come on Saturday.

mistakes.feedback: The subject is {je}: {je remercie}. {vous} is the person thanked.

items.text: Mon grand-père, ___ je parle souvent, habite près de Lyon.
items.gloss: My grandfather, whom I often talk about, lives near Lyon.

mistakes.feedback: You talk about someone with {parler de}, so the word is {dont}.

items.text: Ce ___ est lourd, c'est ce vieux livre ; le livre de Noé est léger.
items.gloss: What's heavy is this old book; Noé's book is light.

mistakes.feedback: No other subject comes before {est}, so it is {ce qui}.

items.text: La boulangerie ouvre à sept heures et elle ___ à vingt heures.
items.gloss: The bakery opens at seven and closes at eight in the evening.

items.instruction: Hugo asks Maya to dance. Say the opposite with {refuser}.

items.text: La voisine ___ habite au premier étage, c'est la dame ___ je t'ai parlé.
items.gloss: The neighbour who lives on the first floor is the lady I told you about.

items.instruction: Noé asks about Saturday. Join the two sentences with {s'il}.
items.shown: Il neige samedi. On reste chez Léa.
items.answer: S'il neige samedi, on reste chez Léa.
accept: On reste chez Léa s'il neige samedi.
Samedi, s'il neige, on reste chez Léa.

mistakes.answer: Si il neige samedi, on reste chez Léa.

items.text: À ___ ! Je passe chez toi samedi prochain.
items.gloss: See you soon! I'll drop by your place next Saturday.

items.question: Maya says {Karim est sympa.} What does she think of him?

items.instruction: Join the two sentences with {où}. Start with {Le jour}.
items.shown: Maya est arrivée un jour. Ce jour-là, il pleuvait.
items.answer: Le jour où Maya est arrivée, il pleuvait.

mistakes.answer: Le jour quand Maya est arrivée, il pleuvait.
mistakes.feedback: After a time word such as {le jour}, French says {où}, not {quand}.

items.text: Le film ___ on regarde ce soir est très long.
items.gloss: The film we're watching tonight is very long.

mistakes.feedback: A new subject comes next, {on}, so the word is {que}, shortened to {qu'}.

items.instruction: Maya asks what is nice round here. Start with {Ce qui} and end with the market.
items.answer: Ce qui est sympa, c'est le marché.

mistakes.answer: Ce que est sympa, c'est le marché.
mistakes.feedback: No other subject comes before {est}, so it is {ce qui}.

items.text: Du jardin ___ Madame Garnier lit le soir, on voit la lune.
items.gloss: From the garden where Madame Garnier reads in the evening, you can see the moon.

items.text: Tu ___ samedi prochain, Hugo ? Ouais, bien sûr !
items.gloss: Are you coming next Saturday, Hugo? Yeah, of course!

items.text: Si vous ___, je passe chez vous samedi, madame.
items.gloss: Léa to Madame Garnier: If you like, I'll drop by your place on Saturday.

mistakes.feedback: Léa says {vous} to Madame Garnier: {si vous voulez}.
